svg.title: What a virtual counselling session requires
svg.desc: Three stacked bands describing what a virtual session needs: a private hour, a device with a connection, and being physically located in British Columbia.
svg.text: What you actually need for a session

text.tspan: Not silent, not beautiful — private. A bedroom with the door shut, a parked car, a booked meeting room. If you are managing
who might overhear, you are not really in the session, and this is the most common practical reason virtual work fails.
A camera and microphone, and a connection good enough for video. Headphones do more for a session than any other single item.
Turning the camera off cuts the bandwidth considerably and is never a problem.
A legal requirement rather than a preference: a counsellor must be registered where the client is physically located during a
session. If you travel or work out of province, say so and it can be planned around.
Where none of the first band is available, a local in-person service is the better referral — and this practice will say so.
